column1: # Blackthorn's audience: the mantra interrogation and its escalation
# (`blackthorn.md` §4). Walking up the approach is enough to trigger it.
# NOT reseeded, deliberately. `qa/tools/reseed.py` replays a scenario's walk
# into a save so both sides start where it was heading, but this scenario
# measures the Blackthorn audience, and `blackthorn.md` §2 makes that a
# **cinematic handler**: it "replace[s] the ordinary map loop while [it]
# runs" and hands back through an explicit scene transition. A cutscene in
# progress is not in `SAVED.GAM`, so a seed written inside one loads as an
# ordinary party standing in the castle and the audience never happens.
# Measured 2026-09-09: a seed taken at the `ask` beat reloads to CASTLE:1 on
# requires-seed: the party on the Blackthorn palace tile at 12:00
# This scenario is flaky, and a run has to be checked before it is believed.
# The audience triggers on walking up the approach, and the walk is scripted
# with fixed waits, so a run whose timing drifts arrives with the trigger
# unmet and simply walks past. Such a run shows `?North` movement echoes in
# the message window instead of the interrogation, and every beat then
# compares unrelated windows. Measured 2026-09-11: two runs minutes apart, one
# with the audience and one without.
# Check the first beat for `Your response?` before reading any result from
# this scenario. A run without it is not evidence about the engine.
# Known gap, measured 2026-09-12: the `ask5` beat reads `offset-1` and nothing
# else. The wording agrees; the original carries one row under the mixer's
# `How much` prompt that this engine does not. `MixPhase::Quantity` is in
# the same prompt, and no scenario yet captures both sides of it - `magic-mix`
# cancels before the quantity stage. The prompt needs its own measurement
# **Walk-up, and therefore timing-sensitive.** This scenario cannot be
# reseeded (see above), so both sides walk to the guard while the resident
# walks its own schedule. Whether the contact fires depends on where that
# resident is when the party arrives, and that depends on real elapsed time
# since launch - which differs between a solo run and a suite run.
# The failure mode is unmistakable and is **not** a wording difference: the
# stock side's window shows only the walk (` North` / ` East` echoes) with no
# demand, while the engine's shows the audience. Measured 2026-09-12, this
# scenario matched twice in isolation and then read `0 beat(s) agree` from
# inside a full-suite run on the same binary, with DOSBox never reaching the
# audience. A run like that has measured nothing; re-run it on its own before
# Not marked as a lottery in the header, deliberately: that would make
# `qa/tools/paired_compare.py` classify every difference here as a re-run and
# stop the suite reporting real regressions in a scenario group that took a
# day to bring to a match.
